newsitem.title: USA: FLO-JO WANTS EXPLANATION FROM CLINTON ON PANEL ROW.
newsitem.headline: FLO-JO WANTS EXPLANATION FROM CLINTON ON PANEL ROW.

text.p: Olympic track star Florence Griffith Joyner said on Friday she wanted an explanation from the White House to why she was dumped from and then reinstated to the President's Council on Physical Fitness.

Joyner, who won four medals at the 1988 Seoul Olympics, had been removed from the council to create a seat for Jake Steinfeld, a California bobdybuilder and television personality who contributed $100,000 to the Democratic Party.

But presidential spokesman Mike McCurry said in New York on Thursday that Clinton would seek to keep Joyner on the council, which is well-known to millions of school children who each year attempt to win a patch by meeting the council's standards on running, push-ups, sit-ups and other tests.

"I just want an explanation," Joyner said on CNN's Inside Politics. "Out of 20 members on the president's council ... only myself has been asked to resign, given no reason why, no explanation, no one has contacted me personally, not the council, not the White House."
Joyner said her husband spoke to one White House official who could tell her nothing useful. She told CNN she would be willing to continue working on the council.

"This is something that I enjoy," she said. "This is something that I have held in great esteem all of my life, and I looked forward to participating in the president's challenge when I was younger. To have been asked by the president to accept that position, that was a dream come true for me."
Steinfeld, best known for his "Body by Jake" cable television programme and videos, gave the hefty campaign contribution last year, when Clinton was re-elected to another four-year term.
Joyner said she could not accept that she was the only person asked to step down.

"It is not unusual with a council like this that serves at the pleasure of the president to rotate members from time to time," McCurry said. Nonetheless, he said later, "...The president believes she should remain as a member of the council."
